"''Correct you are, Obi-Wan. A creature of the same species he is, from Dathomir.|Obi-Wan Kenobi and [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}}}} '''Dathomirian Zabraks''', also known as '''Dathomiri Zabraks''' (shortened as '''Dathomirians''' and '''Dathomiri'''), were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. The creation of the Dathomirian species was the result of [[Hybrid/Legends|hybridization]] between the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] members of the [[Witches of Dathomir]] and their [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[maleling]]s, and thus they were also known as '''Human-Zabrak hybrids''' and '''Zabrak-Humans'''. This resulted in the species' prominent sexual dimorphism, with males and females exhibiting different physical characteristics. Generally, females more closely resembled Humans, while males mostly resembled Zabraks as they possessed cranial horns and had no [[Hair/Legends|hair]]. Members of the female sex had paler skin of [[Color/Legends|white]] or gray varieties, while members of the male sex had skin of red, orange, or yellow shades. The species originated through an unintentional trade cycle, in which [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] raids from the planet [[Rattatak/Legends|Rattatak]] brought numerous Zabrak pirates to Dathomir. These pirates were captured by the [[Witch/Legends|Witches]] of Dathomir, who [[Reproduction/Legends|bred]] with them and conceived Dathomirian Zabraks. By the [[Great Peace of the Republic|era]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the majority of Dathomirian women were members of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Coven/Legends|coven]] of Dathomir Witches. In Nightsister society, Dathomirian malelings were subservient to the Nightsisters as [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] known as [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrothers]]. Some Dathomirian women, like the witch [[Magash Drashi]], were members of other clans such as the [[Singing Mountain Clan]]. The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] had been a Nightbrother during his youth, until he was given to the Sith Lord [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] as an [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] by his mother [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]]. The [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassin]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] was given by the Nightsisters to pirates and grew up on Rattatak. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the Galactic Republic and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], the [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], the leader of the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]], [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|attacked]] the Nightsisters who took refuge in their [[Nightsister fortress|fortress]]. Grievous [[Death/Legends|wiped out]] all the Nightsisters except Talzin and Ventress, the latter of whom had returned to the Nightsisters not long prior, leaving a large portion of the Dathomirian population dead. It was during this period of time when Maul and his brother [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] cut out a path of destruction across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. By the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Nightsisters had been reformed by the Dathomirian [[Gethzerion]]. [[Standard year/Legends|Years]] later, the Dathomirian [[Kaminne Sihn]] led the [[Raining Leaves Clan]] of witches. ==Biology and appearance== {{Quote|You'll have to do ''better than that'', my pale-skinned friend.|Obi-Wan Kenobi, to the Dathomirian Asajj Ventress, on her skin color|{{TCWComicCite|6.14|In the Air}}}} [[File:BoSbow.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Female Dathomirians generally had pale skin.]] Dathomirian Zabraks, also known as Dathomiri Zabraks,[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']] were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Human/Legends|Human]] and [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Hybrid/Legends|hybrids]] [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. They were often simply referred to as Dathomirians[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine 17|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Magazine'' 17]] or Dathomiri, or as Human-Zabrak and Zabrak-Humans in reference to their genetic makeup. Exhibiting [[Gender/Legends|sexual dimorphism]], the male and female sexes had different physical traits. Females generally had [[Color/Legends|pale-gray]] or white skin, while males typically had red, orange, or yellow skin. Unlike members of the male sex, members of the female sex were capable of growing [[Hair/Legends|hair]] atop their heads, in colors such as black, brown, silver, silver-blonde, and white. In general, females could grow eyelashes, while males could grow neither eyelashes nor facial hair.{{TCW|Ambush}} Typically, while females more closely resembled Humans, males more closely resembled Zabraks, bearing cranial horns that grew during the early stages of development in various numbers and patterns. In rarer cases, members of the female sex bore these horns as well. The horns were capable of penetrating skin, such as that of the [[Tholothian/Legends|Tholothian]] species.{{TCW|Revival (episode)}} Dathomirian [[Eye/Legends|eye]] colors included blue, green, grey, red, silver, violet, and yellow. Their eyes were far more sensitive to light than those of a human.''[[Star Wars Collector Edition 2013: The Prequel Trilogy]]'' All Dathomirians were [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force sensitive]] and had a naturally high pain tolerance.''[[Star Wars: The Ultimate Visual Guide: Updated and Expanded]]'' They spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] and [[Dathomiri (language)|Dathomiri]], a [[Language/Legends|language]] likely derived from the [[Paecian/Legends|Paecian]] language of the ancient [[Paecian Empire]], which ruled Dathomir during the [[Old Republic era]].{{CSWECite|III|5|Paecian Empire}} ==Society and culture== {{Main|Witches of Dathomir|Nightsisters/Legends|Nightbrothers/Legends}} {{Quote|In the past, other clans integrated their males as servants or slaves, but our Nightbrothers are kept separated until summoned. In their compound, they naturally form a packlike structure and channel their virile energy into combat training.|Clan Mother Talzin, ''Wild Power''|''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''}} [[File:Unidentified_Nightbrother_Zabrak_7.png|thumb|right|185px|The Nightbrothers (one pictured above) were entirely composed of male Dathomirians.]] The majority of Dathomirians were affiliated with the [[Witches of Dathomir]], a group of [[The Force/Legends|Force-wielders]] who ruled Dathomir and practiced sorcery''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]'' in the form of [[Dathomir Magic]].''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]'' Specifically, the majority were members of the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Coven/Legends|coven]], who practiced solely using the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Dathomiri [[Witch/Legends|witches]] kept [[maleling]]s, a group of males who did not practice magic and were instead used as [[Reproduction/Legends|breeding partners]] for the witches. Dathomirian malelings were referred to as [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrothers]] and were also utilized as [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]]. Because of this system, Dathomirian males rarely met their biological mothers.{{FactFile2014|26|DAT 5-6|Nightsister settlement}} The Nightsisters were capable of performing a transformation spell on a Nightbrother, which would increase the Dathomirian's height, muscle, and horn length. Dathomirians wore tribal [[Tattoo/Legends|tattoos]] in a variety of colors on their faces and bodies to symbolize family loyalty, place of birth, or individual personality. ==History== ===Origins=== {{Quote|Dathomir? The planet of the Witches? I was under the impression that Darth Maul's homeworld was Iridonia.|Obi Wan-Kenobi, to Jedi Masters Yoda and [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]|{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}}}} [[File:RattatakDathomirRelations-Insider122.png|thumb|left|300px|The unintentional trade cycle that led to the hybrid breeding of the Dathomirian species]] Long before the birth of the Dathomirian species, the terms "Dathomirian" and "Dathomiri" were originally used in reference to the culture of Human Witches of Dathomir descended from the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Allya/Legends|Allya]], who was exiled to Dathomir. However, at some point, a [[Star Cruiser/Legends|star cruiser]] from the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' planet [[Iridonia/Legends|Iridonia]] crashed on the Outer Rim{{DB|location|rattatak|Rattatak}} planet [[Rattatak/Legends|Rattatak]], leaving many Iridonian Zabraks stranded. During Rattataki [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] raids on Dathomir, Zabrak pirates were captured and enslaved by the Nightsisters as malelings. The witches discovered that they were genetically compatible with the Zabraks, and isolated them to a smaller region of the planet. The ensuing interbreeding between the two species created the species of hybrids that would become known as Dathomirians.{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/tradingcards/cards/lg_asajjventress.jpg|text=Clone Card: Asajj Ventress (Nightsister)}} Dathomirians became integrated into the Dathomirian witch society, with female Dathomirians joining Humans in their witch clans. In the Nightsister clan ruled by the Dathomirian [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]], the use of "malelings" would be limited only to Dathomirian Zabrak males, called the Nightbrothers. When Talzin united all the Nightsisters into one singular coven, this rule would carry over to the united Nightsisters as well. Over time, the Dathomirians would spread out to other clans.''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]'' At some point between [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],''[[Wild Power]]'', as showcased in ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', mentions the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]''. ''Jedi Alliance'' takes place during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the beginning of which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. The game must also take place before the events of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]] due to the presence of [[Ziro Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Ziro]] within his [[Ziro's Palace/Legends|palace]]. ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film to 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], so the writing of ''Wild Power'' must have taken place afterwards. The book must also have been written prior to the [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|destruction of the Nightsisters]], as shown in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[Massacre]]." {{TCWdates|419}} Therefore, Wild Power must have been written between 22 BBY and 20 BBY. Talzin wrote ''[[Wild Power]]'', a historical record and spiritual manifesto containing detailed descriptions of Dathomirian culture. ===Genocide=== {{Quote|I have learned Ventress has returned to Dathomir. Go there and wipe the witches out. All of them.|Count Dooku, to General Grievous|}} [[File:NightsisterAnnihilation-Massacre.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A group of Nightsisters surrounded by Separatist droids]] In 20 BBY,{{TCWdates|419}} the Nightsisters were [[Battle of Dathomir/Legends|wiped out]] by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], at the order of [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. The attack began with a [[bombing run]] conducted by Grievous' [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]], drawing out the Nightsisters from their [[Nightsister fortress|fortress]]. The following [[Ground warfare/Legends|ground assault]] pitted the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]] against the Nightsisters within the [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]] of Dathomir. Even through the [[Chant of Resurrection/Legends|resurrection]] of the witches' [[Zombie/Legends|zombie]] [[Army of the Dead/Legends|Army of the Dead]] by the elder [[Daka/Legends|Old Daka]], the Nightsisters were forced to retreat and Grievous' army began marching towards the Nightsister fortress. Upon entering the fortress, Grievous killed Old Daka, with Talzin escaping by transforming into her spiritual form of green mist. Following this, the Nightsisters were destroyed with an infinitesimal amount of survivors. The destruction of the Nightsisters also caused the loss of a massive portion of the female Dathomirian population. Sometime around [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]] and [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]],{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=222689&start=07440|thread=Books, Comics, & Television VIPs|user=[[Sue Rostoni]]|date=October 14, 2008|time=11:47 AM}} dates [[Coruscant Nights III: Patterns of Force]] to [[18 BBY/Legends|18.3 BBY]]. [[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']] states that it takes place [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the events of ''Patterns of Force''. Thus ''The Last Jedi'' must take place either in 18 BBY or [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]]. the remaining few Dathomiri Zabrak Nightsisters had lived in conjunction with the mostly Human Nightsisters. By [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]'' to [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]]. the Nightsisters had become almost entirely composed of Humans, with the only known Dathomirian member of the clan left being [[Clan mother/Legends|Clan Mother]] [[Gethzerion]].''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' At some point during or shortly after [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],The afterword of [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] mentions the [[Osarian-Rhommamool conflict|conflict]] between the [[Osarian]] and the [[Rhommamool/Legends|Rhommamool]] as one of the most recent historical events, in the context of the book's [[The Essential Chronology|in-universe nature]]. ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the Osarian-Rhommamool conflict to [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], meaning that the in-universe book must have been released shortly after. the [[Historical Council]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] compiled the historical chronicle ''[[The Essential Chronology]]'', which featured the stories of Gethzerion as well as that of the infamous Dathomirian [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]].[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] In [[36 ABY]], the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]' [[archivist emeritus]] [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] wrote an [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|updated version]], with new additions about the Sith assassin [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] and her various conflicts.''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' ==Dathomirians in the galaxy== {{Quote|Many Zabrak demonstrate strength in the Force. By nature, it would seem.|Darth Sidious, to his master [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], on the Force-sensitivity of Dathomirian Zabraks|[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]}} In the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic community]], Dathomiri were renowned for their impressive pain tolerance, their mental discipline, and their single-mindedness. Members of the species were often considered proud and confident,''[[Star Wars: Beware the Sith]]'' as well as more warlike and dangerous than the other Zabraks of the galaxy.[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]] Notable Dathomirian Nightsisters included Mother Talzin, her [[Talzin's firstborn daughter|firstborn daughter]], Mother Gethzerion, Old Daka, [[Talia (Nightsister)/Legends|Talia]], [[Naa'leth/Legends|Naa'leth]], [[Luce/Legends|Luce]], and [[Karis/Legends|Karis]]. Notable Dathomirian Nightbrothers included [[Feral/Legends|Feral]], the [[Maul's father|father]] of Darth Maul, and [[Viscus/Legends|Viscus]], the leader of the Nightbrothers during the Clone Wars. [[Magash Drashi]] was a Dathomirian Zabrak of the [[Singing Mountain Clan]] under the rule of Mother [[Augwynne Djo]]. [[Kaminne Sihn]] was the Dathomirian leader of the [[Raining Leaves Clan]]. In [[43 ABY]],''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]'' to [[43 ABY]]. Sihn led her clan, most notably during a [[Conclave of the Raining Leaves Clan and the Broken Columns Clan|conclave]] with the [[Broken Columns Clan]] headed by [[Tasander Dest]], which also spelled an interaction with members of the [[New Jedi Order]]. ===The misplaced Nightsister=== {{Quote|She is one of us.|Mother Talzin, to the Nightsisters, upon Asajj Ventress' return to Dathomir|}} [[File:Anakin_vs_asajj.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Asajj Ventress battling Jedi Knight Anakin Skywalker on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]]] Asajj Ventress was born to her Nightsister [[Asajj Ventress's mother/Legends|mother]], but was given to the [[Siniteen/Legends|Siniteen]] pirate [[Hal'Sted/Legends|Hal'Sted]] as a young [[Youngling/Legends|infant]] by Mother Talzin, for the protection of the clan. Hal'Sted brought Ventress to Rattatak, where she was raised by him and the Rattataki Ventress family;[[Republic 60|''Republic'' 60]] however, Hal'Sted was killed in war. The [[Weequay/Legends|Weequay]] who killed him were about to attack Ventress before she was saved by the Jedi [[Ky Narec/Legends|Ky Narec]]. Narec and Ventress went on to become heroes on Rattatak until Narec was killed by a Weequay raider. Eventually, Ventress came under the tutelage of [[Count/Legends|Count]] Dooku, becoming an [[Sith assassin/Legends|assassin]] of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and taking part in the Clone Wars under the command of the Separatists.{{SWE|characters|asajjventress|Asajj Ventress}} She had numerous encounters with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].{{TCW|The Hidden Enemy}}{{TCW|ARC Troopers (episode)}} During the war, Dooku was ordered by his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] to kill Ventress, fearing her growing power in the Force. However, Dooku's efforts failed and, in search of revenge, Ventress returned to Dathomir to request assistance from the Nightsisters. After a failed [[Mission to Serenno (Nightsisters)/Legends|assassination attempt]] on Dooku, Grievous was sent to Dathomir to wipe out the Nightsisters in the Battle of Dathomir. After the battle, Ventress turned to a life of [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]]. She joined a group of fellow bounty hunters hired by the [[Belugan/Legends|Belugan]] [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Rigosso/Legends|Rigosso]] on the world [[Quarzite/Legends|Quarzite]] to safely [[Safe cargo objective/Legends|deliver]] a chest to [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Otua Blank/Legends|Otua Blank]]. Ventress discovered that the chest contained [[Pluma Sodi/Legends|Pluma Sodi]] of the [[Kage Warriors/Legends|Kage Warriors]], a group who opposed the rule of Lord Blank. Sympathizing with the girl's story and finding it similar to her own, she opted to save the girl and instead place the young [[Hunting/Legends|hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] in the chest instead. She acquired the [[Credit chip/Legends|credits]] she was owed and left Quarzite.{{TCW|Bounty (episode)}} Near the end of her time as a bounty hunter, Ventress hunted down Skywalker's [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], who recently had been framed for [[Bombing of the Jedi Temple hangar/Legends|bombing]] the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. Tano struck a deal with Ventress that if she helped the Padawan clear her name, Tano would help her get a pardon from the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], and the two agreed. However, Skywalker arrived at that moment and, believing it was Ventress who framed Tano, he caused the Dathomirian to run off.{{TCW|To Catch a Jedi}} Skywalker returned later, however, and interrogated Ventress, who provided him with information to clear Tano's name.{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}} Sometime later, she returned to the leadership of the Sith and membership of the Separatists under unknown circumstances.''[[Galaxy at War]]'' During her lifetime, Ventress had often been incorrectly referred to as a member of the [[Rattataki/Legends|Rattataki]] species. Rattataki had pale skin{{HolonetOld|biographies|kaliyo-djannis|Kaliyo Djannis}} like female Dathomirians, and Ventress had been raised on Rattatak. ===The Nightbrothers Two=== ====Apprentices==== {{Quote|You instructed me to keep an eye out for beings who might prove helpful. I found such a one on Dathomir not a year ago. A male Dathomiri Zabrak infant.|Darth Sidious, to Darth Plagueis, after finding the young Dathomirian boy Maul|}} [[File:SWDarthPlagueis-BackCover.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ruthless Darth Maul, apprentice to Darth Sidious]] The famous Sith Lord Darth Maul was believed to be a full-blooded Zabrak, though he was in fact a Dathomirian.{{SWE|characters|darthmaul|Darth Maul}} As a boy, he was taken by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Sidious from his mother Talzin[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]] due to his powerful connection to the Force. Over the years, Maul became a weapon of the Sith,''[[The Wrath of Darth Maul]]'' carrying out various missions for his master.[[Darth Maul (2000) 3|''Darth Maul'' (2000) 3]]''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]'' In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], with the Sith ready to reveal themselves to the Jedi, Maul engaged Jedi Master [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], as well as during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]]. While inside the [[Plasma Refinery Complex]] within the city of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] on the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], Maul stabbed and killed Jinn with [[Darth Maul's double-bladed lightsaber/Legends|his lightsaber]]. However, Kenobi was able to defeat the Sith by slicing him in half. Maul fell down into a melting pit and was presumed dead. However, Maul had survived his supposed death, eventually living in the depths of the junk world [[Lotho Minor/Legends|Lotho Minor]]. He fashioned himself a [[Spider/Legends|spider]]-like apparatus in order to allow him to move around, but, over time, his want for vengeance drove him insane.''[[The Clone Wars: The Sith Hunters]]'' Thirteen years later,{{TCWdates|313}} Asajj Ventress required an assassin for her revenge against Dooku. Talzin and the Nightsisters offered Dooku a [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] in [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]], the brother of Maul. Ventress used her control over Opress in order to [[Showdown at Toydaria/Legends|attack]] Dooku. However, the Nightbrother snapped and Ventress lost control over him. Escaping, Opress returned to Dathomir, where Mother Talzin revealed to him that he had a brother, Maul, and gave him a [[Talisman of Finding/Legends|talisman]] to help find him. Opress tracked Maul to Lotho Minor, finding him with a broken mind.{{TCW|Brothers (episode)}} He brought Maul back to Dathomir, where Mother Talzin restored his mind and replaced his six-legged apparatus with two metal legs fashioned from the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] parts left over from the Battle of Dathomir.{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}} ====A new path==== {{Quote|Revenge. I must have revenge.|Maul|}} [[File:SWDarthMaulDeathSentence4.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The two Dathomirian brothers: Maul (front) and Savage Opress (back)]] Reborn, Maul and Opress led a rampage throughout the galaxy with the goal of exacting revenge against the Jedi. Their excursions led them to various worlds, such as [[Orto Norwe]],[[:File:EAOC discussion 2023.jpg|Email from Jason Fry]] [[Pleem's Nexus]], [[Paklan]],[[Darth Maul — Death Sentence 1|''Darth Maul — Death Sentence'' 1]] and [[Moorjhone]].[[Darth Maul — Death Sentence 2|''Darth Maul — Death Sentence'' 2]] They encountered various Jedi, such as Obi-Wan Kenobi, [[Bruu Jun-Fan]], and [[Tatsu]], and additionally fought Asajj Ventress. Upon taking over the [[Ohnaka Gang/Legends|Ohnaka Gang]] of Weequay pirates, Maul and Opress once again [[Skirmish on Florrum/Legends|encountered Kenobi]], this time alongside Jedi Master [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]]. During their confrontation, Opress killed Gallia and, in retaliation, Kenobi cut off Opress's [[Limb/Legends|arm]]. Maul and Opress escaped in an escape pod, injured and exhausted. Drifting aimlessly in [[Realspace/Legends|space]], their escape pod was eventually found by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] splinter group [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], headed by [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]] and his second-in-command [[Bo-Katan Kryze/Legends|Bo-Katan Kryze]]. Taken back to the [[Zanbar Death Watch camp/Legends|Death Watch camp]] on{{TCW|Eminence (episode)}} the [[Swamp/Legends|swamp]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]]{{SWE|locations|zanbar|Zanbar}} [[Zanbar/Legends|Zanbar]], Opress was given a new [[Mechno-arm/Legends|cybernetic arm]] and Maul new [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetic]] legs. Maul and Vizsla discussed their mutual distaste for Kenobi and the Jedi and decided to form an alliance to take over the planet [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] and kill Kenobi. Realizing that their alliance alone would not be enough, Maul created the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]], comprising the Dathomirian brothers and Death Watch, as well as various criminal organizations such as the [[Pyke Syndicate/Legends|Pyke Syndicate]], the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]], and [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]]. Ready to take over Mandalore, Kryze and Vizsla secretly plotted to kill Maul after they have conquered the planet. After [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|gaining]] control over Mandalore, Vizsla and Maul fought in the [[Sundari Royal Palace/Legends|Mandalorian throne room]], where Maul beheaded Vizsla with his own [[Darksaber/Legends|weapon]] and caused Death Watch to split into factions, with [[Mandalorian super commando/Legends|some]] staying loyal to Maul and others detesting his rule.{{TCW|Shades of Reason}} The civil war on Mandalore attracted the attention of the Jedi, who chose not to act until the Senate decided. Kenobi went to Mandalore alone and watched as Maul killed [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], Kenobi's lover and the former [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] of Mandalore, and the Dathomirian had Kenobi locked up.{{TCW|The Lawless}} Darth Sidious sensed a disturbance in the Force and so travelled to Mandalore, where he fought both Maul and Opress, killing the latter but sparing the former. Maul was brought to a [[Spire (Stygeon)/Legends|Separatist prison]] on the planet [[Stygeon/Legends|Stygeon]]. After being broken out by the Shadow Collective, a [[Campaign against the Shadow Collective/Legends|war]] was launched between the Separatists and the Shadow Collective, leaving Talzin dead and the Collective disbanded.[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 1|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 1]][[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 4|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 4]] After his eventual death, Maul was revived by the [[Prophets of the Dark Side]] [[Dark Force|Sith cult]], who had believed that the Sith Lord and apprentice to Sidious, Darth Vader—formerly Anakin Skywalker—would never be able to reach his full potential. Thus, Vader and Maul met on the moon [[Kalakar Six]], where Vader killed Maul and the cultists.{{Tales|9|Resurrection (comic story)}} ==Behind the scenes== ===Origins and appearances=== {{Quote|Why the males of Dathomir are horned Zabraks and the females are smooth-skinned humanoids is something I chose not to address, though I believe the official retcon is that the Dathomiri are a hybrid species descended from both humans and Zabraks.|Daniel Wallace, in his online endnotes for ''Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side''|{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: Book of Sith (part 4)}}}} [[File:Courtship2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Gethzerion's appearance in ''The Courtship of Princess Leia'' retroactively marks the first appearnance of the Dathomirian species.]] Dathomirians first appeared in the [[1994]] novel ''[[The Courtship of Princess Leia]]'', written by [[Dave Wolverton]]. Originally, all the Witches of Dathomir in the book were stated to be humans, until the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the Nightsister Gethzerion to be of the Dathomirian species. Several other characters appearing in early sources were later identified as Dathomirians. Featured in the [[1999]] live-action [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], Darth Maul was referred to as an Iridonian Zabrak by a variety of sources.''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' Asajj Ventress was originally stated to be Rattataki since her debut in the animated television microseries ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'',{{CW|6}} and was also occasionally mistaken to be Human.{{FactFile|116|VEN 1-2|Commander Ventress}} Both of these characters were retconned as Dathomirians during the airing of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''. Prior to these retcons, the species first appeared in "[[Nightsisters (episode)|Nightsisters]]," the twelfth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] of ''The Clone Wars'', which aired on [[January 7]], [[2011]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Episode Guide]]'' The release of the subsequent episode to "Nightsisters," "[[Monster]]," on [[January 14]], 2011, introduced the Dathomirian males, which were described as having been the people from which Darth Maul came. After the episode's release, Maul's [[StarWars.com]] [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]] entry established him as a Dathomirian as well. Having appeared in seasons [[The Clone Wars: Season One|one]] and [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|two]] of ''The Clone Wars'', certain reference books released at the time stated that Ventress was Rattataki.''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: The Visual Guide]]''''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'' However, ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'', a reference book released closer to season three on [[June 21]], [[2010]],{{DK|url=us/9780756663087-star-wars-the-clone-wars-character-encyclopedia|text=Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia|nolive=1}} only lists Ventress' species and homeworld as "Unknown."''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]'' "Nightsisters" confirmed Ventress as Dathomiri, not Ratattaki. ===Naming=== [[File:TCW_Character_Encyclopedia.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Unlike several other preceding character encyclopedias, ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia'' (pictured) opted not to state Asajj Ventress' species, perhaps signaling the forthcoming retcon.]] Released prior to "Nightsisters," the article "[[Everything You Always Wanted to Know about the Nightsisters but Were Afraid to Ask]]," published in the [[Star Wars Insider 122|122nd]] issue of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine on [[December 14]], 2010,{{SWArchive|url=fans/media_news/star_wars_insider_122/index.html|text=Exclusive Howard Chaykin Cover and Poster in ''Star Wars Insider'' #122}} goes into specific detail on the retcon that created the Dathomirian species. It also tackles the sexual dimorphism within the species, as well as identifying them with the species name of "Human-Zabrak hybrids." In his online endnotes for his [[2013]] reference book, ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'', author [[Daniel Wallace]] stated that he deliberately chose not to address the sexual dimorphism present in Dathomirians, but was aware of the official retcon as outlined in ''Insider''. The species was identified as Dathomirians in the accompanying StarWars.com [[Clone Cards]] for Asajj Ventress, Naa'leth, Talia, and Talzin, released in conjunction with "Nightsisters."{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/tradingcards/cards/lg_asajjventress.jpg|text=Clone Card: Asajj Ventress (Nightsister)}}{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/tradingcards/cards/lg_karis.jpg|text=Clone Card: Karis|nobackup=1}}{{SWArchive|url=clonewars/tradingcards/cards/lg_mothertalzin.jpg|text=Clone Card: Mother Talzin|nobackup=1}} The term "Dathomiri" was first used in reference to the species in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.15|fifteenth issue]] of the [[Star Wars Comic#Volume_6|sixth volume]] of the [[Star Wars Comic|''Star Wars'' Comic]] magazine, published by [[Titan Magazines]][[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.15|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.15]] in [[2010#December|December]] 2010.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.15|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.15]] is the [[2010#January|January]] issue of the [[Star Wars Comic|series]] according to its cover, and issues are published in the month prior to the month listed on its cover. Thus, issue 6.15 was published in December. They were first referred to as Dathomiri Zabraks in "[[Restraint]]," a short story written by [[James Luceno]] and published in the second edition of the novel ''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]'' on [[December 27]], 2011.{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/139650/shadow-hunter-star-wars-legends-darth-maul-by-michael-reaves|text=Shadow Hunter: Star Wars Legends (Darth Maul)}} They were identified as Dathomirian Zabraks in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.28|twenty-eighth issue]] of ''Star Wars'' Comic,[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.28|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.28]] published on [[December 15]], 2011.[[Star Wars Comic|''Star Wars'' Comic]] was published every 4 weeks, and issue [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.21|6.21]] was published on [[June 2]], [[2011]] according to {{SWArchive|url=vault/books/whatsnew_may27/index.html|text=What's New This Week: ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic'' #6.21}}. Therefore, issue [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.28|6.28]] was published on approximately [[December 15]], [[2011]]. The 2013 novel [[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']], written by [[Michael Reaves]] and [[Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff]], identified the species with the term Zabrak-Human. ===Distinction between Humans and Dathomirians=== [[File:Backlash_Front.jpg|thumb|right|250px|''Fate of the Jedi: Backlash'', which features Kaminne Sihn and her family]] "Everything You Always Wanted to Know about the Nightsisters but Were Afraid to Ask" states that the Nightsisters comprised mainly Dathomirians. It remains speculation to classify all Witches of Dathomir in the Dathomirian species due to the fact that the planet still remains notably inhabited by pale-skinned female Humans, as shown in ''The Courtship of Princess Leia'' and several other sources. Thus, this article only pertains to individuals confirmed as being a member of the species, even though many other Witches have the same physical traits as Dathomirians. Daniel Wallace and [[Jason Fry]]'s reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' states that Humans made up ninety-seven percent of the population of Dathomir and other species made up only three percent of the population.''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' However, ''The Essential Atlas'' was published in [[2009]],{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/185066/the-essential-atlas-star-wars-by-daniel-wallace-and-jason-fry|text=The Essential Atlas: Star Wars}} a year prior to the foundational Dathomirian retcon in 2010. This article ignores this population statistic, assuming it was retconned as well. ''[[Fate of the Jedi: Backlash]]'', a 2010 novel written by [[Aaron Allston]] and the fourth installment of the ''[[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi]]'' series, features Kaminne Sihn and several members of her family. The listing of Kaminne Sihn as "Dathomiri" in the book's Dramatis Personae section can be deduced to refer to her species and not her culture, given the precedent established with all other characters in the list. The rest of her family members—her [[Kaminne Sihn's father|father]], [[Kaminne Sihn's mother|mother]], sister [[Olianne Sihn]], [[Kaminne Sihn's oldest sister|oldest sister]], and niece [[Sesara Sihn]]—are not explicitly stated to be Dathomirian. Due to the nature of the Dathomirians as hybrids, it is possible that one of her parents is Human and the other is Zabrak, among many other possible explanations making it possible that neither her father nor mother are Dathomirian. As for her sisters and niece, the book does not state whether Kaminne's sisters are full-blooded siblings or half-blooded siblings, meaning none of them are confirmably members of the Dathomirian species. Thus, Kaminne is the only character in ''Backlash'' featured in this article. ===Design and development=== ====Males==== {{Quote|I originally had the horns growing through the skull, but George liked a raised area around them better. I thought of them as weapons; and they do actually look like shark's teeth.|Nick Dudman, on his design for Dathomirian horns|''[[Star Wars: The Making of Episode I The Phantom Menace]]''}} [[File:AoR-DarthMaul-D.png|thumb|left|250px|Iain McCaig's final concept for Maul, with wire-feathers instead of horns]] The look of the Dathomirian species was first brainstormed in the developmental phase of ''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace''. When ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator and film director [[George Lucas]] asked artist [[Iain McCaig]] to draft conceptual designs for a Sith Lord, McCaig arrived at several notable designs. After experimenting with [[Wikipedia:Rorschach test|Rorschach patterns]] for facial tattoos and scars in several "evil [[Senator/Legends|senator]]" designs, McCaig finally arrived at his design for the character who would eventually become Darth Maul during the scripting process.''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]'' He envisioned that Maul would have a face resembling that of "flayed flesh," noting that the pattern of his visage would resemble that of a human face without the skin. He also took inspiration from [[Wikipedia:Aposematism|aposematism]] and [[Wikipedia:List of ethnic groups of Africa|African tribal]] paint, specifically finding the use of a shiny, blood-red pigment terrifying. Combining these concepts, Maul's facial features and skin color were crafted.{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/bts/design/f20000228/index.html|text=Designing a Sith Lord}} In McCaig's original concept, the protrusions atop Maul's head were originally stiffened''[[Star Wars Storyboards: The Prequel Trilogy]]'' feathers rooted in his flesh with wire. These black feathers were inspired by [[Wikipedia:Indigenous peoples of the Americas|Native American]] [[Wikipedia:Totem|prayer totems]]. He envisioned that, every morning, Maul would bind the feathers into his head. However, the feathers were misinterpreted by Lucasfilm Creative Effects Supervisor [[Nick Dudman]] as biological horns. Lucas briefly considered making Maul, and thus all his features, female. During the production portion of filming for ''The Phantom Menace'', the original horns designed by Dudman were intended to grow through Maul's skull, but Lucas instead suggested that the horns were instead protruded from a slightly raised area. Dudman envisioned the Dathomirian horns as weapons similar in appearance to [[Wikipedia:Shark tooth|shark teeth]]. The makeup designers crafted the horns themselves out of rubber, and used alcohol-based pigments for Maul's Dathomirian skin and tattoos.''[[Star Wars Chronicles: The Prequels]]'' The design and likeness of Darth Maul would serve as the template for the other male Dathomirians introduced in ''The Clone Wars''. Once Feral's model was created for "Monster," his build and likeness were used for the other Nightbrothers.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Three|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Three]] The male Dathomirian design recalls [[Wikipedia:Christian demonology#Appearance|horned demonic imagery]] originating from the [[Wikipedia:Witch trials in the early modern period|European witch trials of the seventeenth century]].''[[Star Wars: The Power of Myth]]'' ====Females==== {{Quote|The original Ventress design proposed for Episode II was this sort of pale-faced, vaguely samurai-looking female character, that was similar to another design for Episode I for a Sith Witch. And neither of those designs made it into the live-action films, but they were both interesting concepts and added to George's huge pile of interesting artwork for future use. Ventress was now officially a Nightsister herself, which gives you an instant history that hadn't been there in the past and sort of meant that the way she looked made sense.|[[Kilian Plunkett]], Lead Designer for ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars''|}} [[File:SithWitch.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Iain McCaig's "Sith Witch" concept art (above) was one of several scrapped designs used to create the character of Asajj Ventress.]] The origins of the design for female Dathomirians also trace back to ''The Phantom Menace''. When Lucas asked McCaig for a design for the Sith Lord who would later become Maul, he instructed McCaig to draw his "worst nightmare." From this instruction, he drafted a concept of a white-skinned humanoid with red hair titled "[[Nightsister Sith witch|Sith Witch]]," which was deemed too scary and was thus scrapped. McCaig described this design as a "lifeless face pressed against the window," and with the appearance of something between dead and alive. During the conceptual portion of the succeeding [[2002]] prequel trilogy film, [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], concept artist [[Dermot Power]] crafted several designs for a "Sith Warrior." These drawings depicted a female humanoid with white skin, blue highlights, smaller skin markings, and a samurai build. Some designs kept this character bald, while others opted to place a helmet or cloak upon her head to obscure her features.''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]'' [[File:Assajj_concept-art.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Dermot Power's ''Attack of the Clones'' concept art for a "Sith Warrior"]] Lucasfilm concept artists noticed the similar appearance of the two concept designs and combined them into the character of Asajj Ventress. For her debut in [[2003]]'s ''Clone Wars'', the design team opted to take these concepts and slim down Ventress's structure, with the goal to make her more skeletal-like.[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Volume One|''Star Wars: Clone Wars'' Volume One]] For Ventress' reintroduction into [[2008]]'s ''The Clone Wars'', concept artist [[Alex Woo]] made several tweaks to her design to make her appear more seductive. Even prior to the official retcon, Woo decided to change Ventress's facial tattoos''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' in order to make them look similar to those of Darth Maul.{{StoryCite|story=The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars (booklet)|book=Star Wars: The Clone Wars Seasons 1-5 Collector's Edition|bformatted=''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Seasons 1-5 Collector's Edition|sformatted=''The Art of Star Wars: The Clone Wars''|smanual=1}} The show's later introduction of the Nightsisters as Ventress's people thus took the vague features of her appearance and implemented them into the rest of the female Dathomirians. Mother Talzin in particular was inspired by McCaig's second "Sith Witch" concept for ''The Phantom Menace'',{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode312.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Nightsisters}} a design which already shared many biological features with Ventress's designs. ===Non-canon depictions=== {{Quote|From there the main character really wasn't Maul but was an heir of his that was basically just like him. I'm Dan Borth of Red Fly Studio the creators of the cancelled Darth Maul game Ask Me Anything|user=[[Dan Borth|Rancor_lover]]|date=2015-10-24|archiveurl=https://archive.is/fxUli}}}} [[File:Mr._Garfield.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jedi Master Garfield during the [[195 BBY]] school year]] The [[Canon|non-canon]] ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Academy]]'' series introduced two Zabrak characters, Jedi Master [[Garfield]] and Jedi Padawan [[Cyrus (Jedi Academy)|Cyrus]], in it's first book [[Jedi Academy (novel)|''Jedi Academy'']],[[Jedi Academy (novel)|''Jedi Academy'']] written by [[Jeffrey Brown]] and released in 2013.{{Amazon|url=Trilogy-Box-Set-Star-Wars/dp/0545854415|text=''Star Wars: Jedi Academy Trilogy Box Set''}} While the skin color of Cyrus and Garfield were indecipherable from the contents of the book itself, the cover depicted the two with red skin and Dathomirian characteristics.
